model: Liebert DataMate / Mini-Mate2 (MM2 controller, IS-WEBADPT card)
applies_to: Liebert DataMate and Mini-Mate2 units with the MM2 controller, read through the IS-WEBADPT / OC485-ADPT card.
summary: The Liebert DataMate / Mini-Mate2 map is a short legacy list: unit status, temperature and humidity readings and setpoints, an on/off control word and alarm words where several alarms share one object as bits. Only use it with the card variant named in the title.
notes: Tables 5.38, pdf pages 1482-1484 of the 2024 guide (printed page numbers are 4 lower).
Object names are Vertiv data IDs (e.g. 5331_1); the description holds the guide's data label. Labels repeated for different sensors or circuits get the group name in brackets.
This table has no access column; the Control Points objects are assumed writable and everything else read-only.
The guide lists each alarm bit as its own row (object names such as ba01_1:00); here each object appears once with its bits in the states text.

source.title: Liebert IntelliSlot Modbus/BACnet Reference Guide (Modbus RTU and TCP, BACnet MSTP and IP)

integration.summary: Fit a Liebert IntelliSlot IS-WEBADPT card (BACnet IP only), give it a unique device instance and let it discover the unit; the objects are then created automatically. Map the on/off and setpoint objects if the BMS controls the unit, and the status, main measurements and event objects for monitoring.
setup: The card needs a unique Device Instance Number; the device object represents the card, not the unit.
The cards have no BBMD; IS-UNITY-DP and IS-IPBML support foreign device registration (BBMD address and time-to-live).
IS-UNITY-DP adds BACnet MS/TP; IS-WEBADPT and IS-IPBML are BACnet IP only. Check the compatibility table (guide section 1.1.3) for the card your unit supports.
gotchas: Vertiv asks for no more than about two writes and two reads per second on average; do not rewrite setpoints continuously.
No segmented responses: large ReadPropertyMultiple requests can fail, so split them.
Only data the managed unit actually has is created on the card, so object counts vary by model and options.

points.name: ba01_1
points.states: Bit 0 = Communications; Bit 1 = Local Off; Bit 2 = Remote Off; Bit 3 = High Head Pressure 1; Bit 5 = Loss of Airflow; Bit 7 = Change Filters; Bit 8 = High Temperature; Bit 9 = Low Temperature

points.name: ba02_1
points.states: Bit 0 = High Humidity; Bit 1 = Low Humidity; Bit 2 = Humidifier Problem; Bit 8 = Smoke Detected; Bit 9 = Loss of Water Flow

points.name: ba03_1
points.states: Bit 1 = Short Cycle; Bit 2 = Loss of Power; Bit 6 = Local Alarm 1; Bit 7 = Local Alarm 2; Bit 8 = High Water

points.name: bc01_1
points.states: Bit 0 - ON = Unit Off Bit 1 - ON = Unit On
